svg.title: Gradient Propagation and Branch Depth
svg.desc: Input gradient versus branch depth, comparing an FNN and a residual block. Each integer depth is a different number of scalar layers in the branch. The residual block has one identity shortcut around the whole branch. Both receive an incoming gradient of one. With the same local derivative s at each layer, blue is s to the power n, orange is the same branch contribution, green is the direct identity contribution of one, and the total is one plus s to the power n. Each local derivative is s=0.5. Below, both number lines show one ordinary SGD update of an earlier weight, starting at w=1 with X=w and learning rate 0.01. The ordinary update shrinks with depth while remaining nonzero. The residual-block update includes the direct identity contribution. These are independent updates at each depth. Lines interpolate between integer depths. This is not a training experiment or a plot of intermediate gradients inside a fixed network.
